nodes.title: Introduction to energy production in the mitochondria
nodes.canonical_question: How do mitochondria produce energy for the cell?
nodes.summary: Cellular respiration converts nutrients into ATP. Most ATP is made in the mitochondrion.

nodes.title: The electron transport chain
nodes.canonical_question: How does the electron transport chain move electrons and build a gradient?
nodes.summary: Membrane complexes pass electrons and pump protons. Oxygen is the final electron acceptor.

nodes.title: Proteins essential for ATP synthesis
nodes.canonical_question: Which proteins are essential for ATP synthesis in the mitochondrion?
nodes.summary: ATP synthase has a proton-driven rotor and a catalytic head. Complexes I to IV build the proton gradient that drives it.

nodes.title: Cytochrome c: structure and role
nodes.canonical_question: What does cytochrome c do in the electron transport chain?
nodes.summary: Cytochrome c is a small mobile electron carrier. It shuttles electrons from Complex III to Complex IV.

nodes.title: Electron donation to Complex IV
nodes.canonical_question: How does cytochrome c donate electrons to Complex IV?
nodes.summary: Cytochrome c docks on Complex IV and releases its electron. The electron moves through copper and heme sites to oxygen.

nodes.title: Plant mitochondria different from animal
nodes.canonical_question: Are plant mitochondria different from animal mitochondria?
nodes.summary: Plant and animal mitochondria share the same central chain. Plants add alternative electron routes that trade ATP for flexibility.

nodes.title: Building the proton gradient
nodes.canonical_question: How is the proton gradient across the inner membrane built?
nodes.summary: Complexes pump protons as electrons move along the chain. The build-up stores energy across the inner membrane.
